chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Mu'awiyah ibn 'Ammar, who said:

I asked Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام about a man who comes to the mosque while they are in the salat, and the Imam has preceded him by one rak'ah or more; then the Imam becomes ill, takes him by the hand, and since he is the nearest of the people to him, brings him forward.

He عليه السلام said: He completes the salat with the people, then he sits. When they have finished the tashahhud, he signals to them with his hand to the right and the left, and it is as though his signaling to them with his hand stands in place of the tashahhud and the completion of their salat. Then he completes what he had missed, or what remained upon him.

key_terms.التَّشَهُّدِ: the sitting testimony near the end of the salat
key_terms.الشِّمَالِ: the left side, indicating the other direction of the concluding gesture
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: the ritual prayer being discussed in congregational form
key_terms.الْإِمَامُ: the prayer leader who becomes unable to continue
key_terms.الْمَسْجِدَ: the mosque where the congregational salat is being performed
key_terms.الْيَمِينِ: the right side, indicating one direction of the concluding gesture
key_terms.بِرَكْعَةٍ: one unit of prayer that the replacement leader had missed

ai.seo_question: What should be done if the Imam becomes unable to continue and appoints someone who joined late to complete the congregational salat?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the ruling for a congregational salat in which the Imam becomes unable to continue and appoints a latecomer who has missed one or more rak'ahs to lead the remainder. The appointed person completes the congregational salat for the people, signals their conclusion, and then finishes the rak'ahs he himself had missed.
